LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 13.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Savings Suggested vocabulary wealth, income, needs, wants, spend, cost, save, po
Topic 13.1: Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary, part of Savings Suggested vocabulary wealth, income, needs, wants, spend, cost, save, po in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we use sounds to learn new words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Listen and pick out words with the target letter sound combinations (-lf, -rf, spl-) from an audio clip/ poem/ story. Learners with speech difficulties can pick orally, by typing or writing.

2. Practise saying words with the target sounds with peers.

3. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

4. Generate and list words with the target sounds.

5. Categorise different words according to each of the target sounds. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Listen and pick out words with the target letter sound combinations (-lf, -rf, spl-) from an audio clip/ poem/ story. Learners with speech difficulties can pick orally, by typing or writing.
2. Practise saying words with the target sounds with peers.
3. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.
4. Generate and list words with the target sounds.
5. Categorise different words according to each of the target sounds. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and engagingly is enhanced as they use new words learnt in

communication.

Values:
Peace: Love is enhanced as learner works harmoniously with peers during role plays activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Socio-economic issues (Financial Literacy): The learner acquires financial management skills as they learn vocabulary related

to savings.

Link to other Learning areas:

The learner uses the skills of correct pronunciation of words in pronouncing words in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital
